trails.title: The Mekong Journey
trails.subtitle: Six stops through monsoon lands and island chains

stops.prompt: Find Vietnam — the long S-shaped country on the eastern coast, east of Laos and Cambodia.
stops.hint: Look for a long thin S shape hugging the South China Sea.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Correct — Vietnam runs along the eastern coast, east of Laos and Cambodia.

stops.prompt: Laos and Thailand: which country is bigger?
stops.hint: Read the Area rows — the numbers are there to compare.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Right — Thailand is more than twice the size of Laos.

stops.prompt: Which place fits all the clues?
stops.hint: One of these is smaller than 1,000 km² — a whole country smaller than many farms.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Yes — Singapore is a tiny island city-state just south of Malaysia.

stops.prompt: Find Indonesia — the huge archipelago south-east of Malaysia.
stops.hint: Look for many islands: Sumatra, Java, Borneo and Sulawesi.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Correct — Indonesia is the world's largest archipelago, stretched along the equator south-east of Malaysia.

stops.prompt: The Philippines and Malaysia: which has more people?
stops.hint: Read the People rows — both numbers are in millions.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Right — the Philippines has about 117 million people, more than three times Malaysia's.

stops.prompt: Which country fits all the clues?
stops.hint: The Mekong river flows through the answer.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Yes — Laos is the landlocked country north of Cambodia, and the Mekong runs through it.

trails.title: Following the Nile
trails.subtitle: From the Mediterranean shore to the great lakes

stops.prompt: Find Egypt — the country where the Nile meets the Mediterranean Sea.
stops.hint: Follow the river line north to the sea coast.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Correct — Egypt lies on the Mediterranean, and the Nile runs all the way through it.

stops.prompt: Egypt and Libya: which country is bigger?
stops.hint: Read the Area rows — one is nearly twice the other.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Right — Libya is nearly twice the size of Egypt, but far fewer people live there.

stops.prompt: Which country fits all the clues?
stops.hint: The answer touches the Indian Ocean.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Yes — Kenya reaches from Ethiopia down to the Indian Ocean coast.

stops.prompt: Tanzania and Uganda: which has more people?
stops.hint: Both are in the tens of millions — read closely.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Right — Tanzania has about 67 million people, more than Uganda.

stops.prompt: Find Madagascar — the big island east of Tanzania, across the channel.
stops.hint: It is the large island off the east coast, shaped like a long footprint.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Correct — Madagascar sits in the Indian Ocean east of the mainland.

stops.prompt: Which country fits all the clues?
stops.hint: The Blue Nile begins in the answer's highlands.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Yes — Ethiopia is a big landlocked highland country where the Blue Nile begins.

trails.title: Andes & Amazon
trails.subtitle: The long cordillera and the great rainforest river

stops.prompt: Find Peru — on the Pacific coast, north of Chile.
stops.hint: Follow the Pacific coast up from the long thin country.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Correct — Peru sits on the Pacific coast with the Andes running through it.

stops.prompt: Bolivia and Brazil: which country is bigger?
stops.hint: One of them covers nearly half the continent.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Right — Brazil is nearly eight times the size of Bolivia — the giant of the continent.

stops.prompt: Which country fits all the clues?
stops.hint: The answer is long and thin, squeezed between mountains and sea.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Yes — Chile is the long thin country between the Andes and the Pacific.

stops.prompt: Ecuador and Colombia: which has more people?
stops.hint: Read the People rows — one is close to three times the other.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Right — Colombia has about 52 million people, nearly three times Ecuador's.

stops.prompt: Find Brazil — the largest country, east of the Andes.
stops.hint: It covers most of the eastern half of the map.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Correct — Brazil covers nearly half of South America.

stops.prompt: Which country fits all the clues?
stops.hint: The answer has giant salt flats high in the mountains.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Yes — Bolivia is landlocked high in the Andes, with peaks over 6,000 m.

trails.title: Across the Alps
trails.subtitle: Old towns between the Atlantic and the Alps

stops.prompt: Find Italy — the boot that reaches into the Mediterranean.
stops.hint: Look for a shape like a boot kicking a small triangle.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Correct — Italy is the boot-shaped peninsula in the middle of the Mediterranean.

stops.prompt: France and Germany: which has more people?
stops.hint: Both are large countries — read the People rows.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Right — Germany has about 84 million people; France has about 68 million.

stops.prompt: Which country fits all the clues?
stops.hint: The answer is famous for mountains, watches and lakes.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Yes — Switzerland is the small landlocked country high in the Alps.

stops.prompt: Italy and Greece: which has more people?
stops.hint: One of these has nearly six times the other.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Right — Italy has about 59 million people — nearly six times Greece's.

stops.prompt: Find Greece — the mainland and islands in the south-east, south of the Alps.
stops.hint: Look at the bottom of the map, among the many small islands.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Correct — Greece lies in the south-east, where the Aegean Sea meets the land.

stops.prompt: Which country fits all the clues?
stops.hint: The answer is famous for steep sea inlets called fjords.
stops.feedbackCorrect: Yes — Norway runs down the western side of the Scandinavian peninsula, famous for its fjords.
